responses.reason: Distribution revenue moved $5,398,000 to $5,905,000, the $507,000 cited, and share gains in the independent restaurant channel are asserted with no customer or channel split behind them; S1 goes further and says the channel mix did not move, so the memo offers a channel story and a no-channel-change story for the same month.

The invoices are for August freight, so the cost belongs in August and an accrual of $31,200 should have been posted at the close rather than left to a September portal; adding it would take the account from $27,600 up to roughly $58,800 and change the size of the movement being explained.

Unrounded, July margin is $1,267,000 over $5,398,000, which is 23.5 percent, and August is $1,293,000 over $5,905,000, which is 21.9 percent, so margin fell 1.6 points; cost of product sold rose 11.6 percent while revenue rose only 9.4 percent, and the conclusion that mix did not move does not survive that.

S10 says no new legal matters arose during August while S11 books $185,000 for a delivery claim notified to the broker in August, and I believe S11 because the accrual is actually posted in the table; the difference matters because the memo would otherwise send a reader past the largest single movement in the month with a sentence saying there is nothing to see.

The account fell $96,400 to $28,900, a decline of $67,500, and releasing a July accrual reduces expense rather than becoming August expense, so the sentence is self-contradictory; if the show is in September the cost belongs in September and the July accrual should either stand or be reversed cleanly, not described as both.

Warehouse wages fell $37,700 while temporary labor at the same depot rose $86,800, so the whole of the wage decline is plausibly work moving to agency staff and net labor is actually up $49,100; take the substitution out and there is no productivity saving left to report, which makes S8 an operating conclusion the numbers do not support.

Supplier rebates went $42,000 to $214,000, which is $172,000 and 409.5 percent, clearing the dollar leg and the percent leg together, and a swing of that size in other income with no sentence at all cannot go out; I would ask for the rebate agreements, the volumes that triggered them and the entries posted in August.

Insurance moved exactly zero, which fails both legs of the threshold, so no commentary and no controller confirmation are owed on this line at all; the challenge is asking me to chase a nil variance while $172,000 of rebates and $481,000 of product cost sit in the memo with no driver, and it only restates what S7 already says.

Depot repairs moved $36,400 to $44,800, which is $8,400 and fails the $25,000 dollar leg even though 23.1 percent clears the percent leg, and the memo states plainly that both must pass, so the silence on this line is correct and no contractor schedule is owed before release.

Service revenue went $1,096,000 to $985,000, so the account fell $111,000 and 10.1 percent rather than growing, and once the direction flips the renewals story argues the opposite of the table, leaving a required line explained backwards and a revenue decline unaddressed.

This schedule carries July and August only and there is no June column anywhere in it, so the $91,200 the challenge calls a June balance is not in front of me; on the two months actually shown fleet fuel moved $122,800 to $129,400, which is $6,600 and 5.4 percent, failing both legs, and nothing here evidences a third month of cutoff trouble.

Bad debt moved $1,700 and 17.9 percent, so it clears the percent leg but fails the $25,000 dollar leg and should not be in the memo at all; the three clauses it spends on one Southline account displaced supplier rebates at $172,000 and cost of product sold at $481,000, both of which clear the threshold and get nothing.

The productivity program is offered in S8 for warehouse wages and then reused in S12 for shrink, but a program launched at the start of the month cannot credibly cut shrink 62.9 percent in its first month, and S6 aside the July balance of $71,200 looks like the real anomaly, so what is unexplained is whether August is a genuine fall or the reversal of a July overstatement.

findings: Account 4300 Supplier rebates: $214,000 of rebates earned on purchases is classified as other income and held outside the margin calculation in the same month cost of product sold rose $481,000, which flatters the margin discussion in S1; rebates on inventory purchases normally reduce cost of product sold and the challenge list asks only for a driver, not for the classification

Account 5000 Cost of product sold rose $481,000, 11.6 percent, clearing both legs of the threshold, and no sentence in the memo gives that movement a driver of its own; S1 uses the account only as an input to the margin claim
